Statin are lipid lowering medications that are used in treatment of hyperlipidemia and atherosclerosis

Examples of these medications include atorvastatin, rosuvastatin, simvastatin and fluvastatin

And here we will talk about what does these medications do to your body

Administration

Statins are taken orally, they would go through the mouth , pharynx, esophagus, stomach and intestine where they got absorbed

After that they got distributed into the body tissues

Mechanism of action

After distribution statins work by

Statins work by inhibiting an enzyme called HMG CoA reductase =>this enzyme is involved in the production of cholesterol in the liver=> once this enzyme is inhibited, this lead to lowering the production of cholesterol

As a result there is lower total cholesterol, lower LDL concentrations (bad lipids) while increasing the HDL

Metabolism

After that they got metabolized in the liver by CYP and after that they get excreted through urine and bile

Side effects

Now statins are usually well tolerated but sometimes they may lead to side effects

Myopathy: damage to the muscles, manifest as muscle pain or weakness, treated by stopping the medication

Hepatotoxicity: elevation of liver enzymes with statin use is a possible side effect, this might lead to hepatocellular liver injury, manifest as weakness, fatigue, jaundice or dark colored urine

Diabetes mellitus, statin therapy also associated with increased risk of developing a new onset diabetes

Statin rarely associated with statin associated cognitive dysfunction
